stories.title: Decision theatre or decision design?
stories.summary: A 2025 survey by BetterUp Labs and the Stanford Social Media Lab found 40 percent of US desk workers experienced workslop, defined as AI-generated content that appears polished but fails to advance tasks. As machines generate more information, the challenge of decision-making remains for human workers.

stories.title: Research-in-the-loop and the speed of AI
stories.summary: As AI agents automate code generation, software development is shifting toward a model where learning occurs after the output is produced. Much like the transition from film to digital photography, the cost of each iteration has dropped, changing how teams approach research and usability testing.

stories.title: Journey mapping as a narrative tool
stories.summary: Journey maps visualize a person's process to achieve a goal by compiling user actions into a timeline. By incorporating thoughts and emotions, these tools transform raw data into a narrative of the user experience. The practice remains a standard method for condensing complex information into actionable insights.

stories.title: The human appeal of the imperfect
stories.summary: Designers have spent years refining machines to achieve flawless output. Recent trends suggest that this perfection is now perceived as an absence of character. The crooked plate is being reconsidered as a more human alternative to the algorithmic aesthetic.

stories.title: The design workflow in the AI era
stories.summary: Vitalii Khomenko, principal designer at Orizon Design, argues that the focus on engineering-side solutions for speed is outdated. He suggests that design workflows must be restructured to accommodate the AI era, warning that the window for teams to adapt is narrower than many founders anticipate.

stories.title: Frontend development and design systems
stories.summary: While artificial intelligence has accelerated code generation, the process of translating design concepts into digital experiences remains dependent on manual handoffs. Marketing and design teams continue to define layouts that developers must convert, limiting autonomy and affecting delivery times for new campaigns and adaptations.

stories.title: Gen Z apps inspire museum wayfinding
stories.summary: Hackney studio Fieldwork Facility drew inspiration from Gen Z apps to design wayfinding for the V&A East Storehouse. The project aims to make the museum's vault of 250,000 historic objects accessible to younger, more diverse audiences who may otherwise feel excluded from traditional institutional environments.

stories.title: The development of Atkinson Hyperlegible
stories.summary: Graphic designer Megan Eiswerth contributed to the Atkinson Hyperlegible typeface, developed for the Braille Institute of America. The font, which received a 2024 Innovation by Design Award, was added to the Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum collection. The type family remains free for public use.

stories.title: Triage algorithms lack user-centered design
stories.summary: A systematic review in Frontiers in Digital Health found that machine learning systems for emergency department triage rarely incorporate iterative usability testing or structured interface design. Despite extensive research into clinical AI, these predictive tools often fail to integrate human-centered design principles into their clinician displays.

stories.title: Older adults and robotic exercise coaches
stories.summary: Research into robotic exercise coaches for older adults shows a divide between favorable survey ratings and actual home adoption. While participants appreciate the technology, practical design concerns remain. The study highlights the need for solutions that address mobility and fall risks without intimidating users in home settings.

stories.title: Hand-formed ribbon branding for Julia
stories.summary: Hey Studio created the brand identity for the coffee shop Julia by photographing real ribbon to form the wordmark. By using hand-formed letters, the design retains folds, creases, and shadows. The identity centers on the act of tying a bow, applied across the shopfront and materials.

stories.title: Toronto Symphony Orchestra identity update
stories.summary: Underline Studio reimagined the Toronto Symphony Orchestra identity by centering it on an animated S that responds to live music. The monogram features an echoing serif S flanked by static T and O characters. The system aims to connect audiences more closely with orchestral performance.

stories.title: Philadelphia Museum of Art brand identity
stories.summary: Gretel redesigned the Philadelphia Museum of Art identity using a griffin motif redrawn from a 1938 original. The badge features the griffin within a black roundel, accompanied by custom typography. The museum briefly shortened its name in 2025 before restoring the full title in 2026.

stories.title: Editorial design for Die neue Polis
stories.summary: Studio unfolded designed the editorial layout for NZZ Libro's Die neue Polis using a typography-only approach. The design places bold italic blurbs directly on the front cover, treating the text as the primary visual element. The book examines Swiss political and historical debates without photography.

stories.title: Ardor retro computer UI design
stories.summary: Viacheslav Sheikin designed the UI for Ardor Retro Computer to stage a cloud AI agent on a phosphor CRT display. The interface features scanlines and keyboard-driven controls, moving away from standard SaaS pricing grids to present connected devices as rotatable 3D objects within a terminal view.

stories.title: Porto Rocha designs Almeida & Dale identity
stories.summary: Porto Rocha developed the brand identity for gallery Almeida & Dale using a custom typeface and a specific blue color palette. The system, which includes catalogues and fair posters, prioritizes the artwork in every layout. The gallery is currently the largest in Latin America.

stories.title: Pen typeface mimics ink pooling
stories.summary: Typeface makers DDOTT and Morula released Pen, a font designed to replicate the small ink stains that occur when a pen nib pauses on paper. The letterforms are based on industrial drafting scripts, with visual corrections applied to maintain consistent stroke thickness across the character set.

stories.title: Shahnameh heroes reimagined as calendar
stories.summary: Designer Nigora Nasimova created Shahnameh-2026, a calendar project that integrates Persian miniature paintings and the epic tales of Ferdowsi into modern graphic design. The project was developed as a response to creative burnout, aiming to bring regional cultural heritage into the context of contemporary life.

stories.title: Monotype Expands Inkwell with Four New Styles Inspired by the Freedom of Handwriting - StreetInsider
Meevaa Foods brand manual ranks among world's top 30
stories.summary: Meevaa Foods by Zappfresh has been recognised on Branding Style Guides, an international archive of identity systems. The company's 68-page guidebook is now listed among the 30 most popular brand manuals worldwide. The archive is used by designers, agencies, marketers and design students.

stories.title: Google Labs updates Stitch interface design tool
stories.summary: Stitch turns text, sketches and wireframes into web and mobile designs with frontend code. Introduced in 2025, the tool now supports multiple artboards and a brand specification file format. Gemini 2.5 Pro interprets inputs to generate interface proposals, structure and components for the user.

stories.title: Adobe adds Firefly Design and Graph tools in beta
stories.summary: Adobe is expanding Firefly with a shared canvas for creative work and a workflow automation tool. The company is also introducing beta assistants that accept written instructions for multi-step tasks. Connections allowing outside agents to edit local Creative Cloud projects are currently in preview.

stories.title: Figma and Stanford researchers release animation benchmark
stories.summary: Researchers from Figma and Stanford University have introduced MotionGraphicsBench to evaluate how large language models animate static vector graphics. The benchmark uses programmatic verification to assess 100 tasks, moving away from subjective human scoring. It provides fine-grained evaluation code for multimodal artificial intelligence researchers.

stories.title: Video | Adobe MAX 2026 Explained: Firefly Goes Agentic, Premiere Pro Gets AI Upgrades & More! - NDTV
Canva launches Craft AI image generator
stories.summary: Canva has released its first AI image-generation model, Canva Craft. The company claims its research lab is the world's second most advanced for image generation, trailing only OpenAI. A recent reviewer comparison found the model produced similar results to ChatGPT across several visual prompts.

stories.title: Canva introduces Craft AI image generation model
stories.summary: Canva has launched Canva Craft, an AI model designed to generate visual content for marketing and social media. The company claims its new tool is second only to OpenAI. It is intended to integrate image generation directly into the existing Canva design workflow.

stories.title: Adobe previews experimental AI research at MAX Sneaks
stories.summary: Adobe showcased ten experimental research projects at its annual conference, including tools for relighting and brush-based image understanding. These previews are not finished features, but the company notes that past research projects have frequently influenced the final direction of its creative software.

stories.title: Adobe announces AI agent integration across creative suite
stories.summary: Adobe is integrating AI agents into Firefly, Creative Cloud and GenStudio to automate repetitive tasks and natural language editing. The company is also expanding partnerships with Google and Microsoft to embed its tools into third-party applications. Adobe aims to become a more automated creative toolbox.

stories.title: Adobe to allow external AI agents to edit native files
stories.summary: Adobe plans to enable external AI agents to edit native Photoshop, Illustrator and Premiere files while maintaining layer and sequence integrity. A private beta for these local integrations is scheduled for early 2027. Adobe's own internal Creative Agent is already available in beta.

stories.title: Adobe adds interactive 3D-like scene tools to Photoshop
stories.summary: Adobe is testing experimental tools that allow creators to navigate within still photographs. The Photoshop beta now includes Camera Angles, which lets users explore new viewpoints and render alternate compositions. The company says this technology expands a single photograph into a flexible creative scene.

stories.title: Adobe demonstrates 3D scene navigation from single photos
stories.summary: At Adobe MAX, the company showcased a research project that infers depth and context from a single photograph. The tool allows a camera to move above, below and behind subjects in a still image. The demonstration was part of the annual showcase of research in progress.

stories.title: Runway releases open-source robot model Praxis-1
stories.summary: Runway has released its robot model Praxis-1 under an Apache 2.0 license. The model processes camera images and text to calculate robot movements. While it can be adapted through additional training, the company notes the model occasionally confuses similar objects and struggles with complex planning.

stories.title: Adobe’s Next Decade Depends on Being Everywhere Creative Work Happens - The AI Economy | Ken Yeung
Substack adds website themes and design controls
stories.summary: Substack has launched new website design tools including seven themes and layout controls. Publishers can now customize typography and colors through a mini-editor. A shuffle feature allows for random combinations of settings, though the changes apply only to the web version and not the app.

stories.title: Testing AI app builders for usability and cost
stories.summary: A test of 10 AI app builders found that most can generate functional software from a single prompt. Differences in cost and code maintenance emerge after repeated edits. The evaluation compared tools based on usability, correctness and the effort required to fix generated code.

stories.title: Adobe makes MAX 2026 sessions available on demand
stories.summary: Adobe has released 13 video sessions from its 2026 conference for on-demand viewing. The collection focuses on video editing, color grading and experimental projects from Adobe Labs. The sessions cover a range of professional workflows and creator rights topics.

stories.title: Canva claims its Craft model beats frontier AI labs
stories.summary: Canva says its Craft model plans designs using data from 250 million creatives. Stefano Corazza, head of AI research, argues the company can beat frontier labs because it owns the editing surface where creative work happens. Having the data is apparently the same as having the intelligence.

stories.title: Printify adds AI image generation to its platform
stories.summary: Printify has added trend-based style templates to its AI image generator, allowing merchants to turn short prompts into print-ready designs. The company says style templates give merchants a stronger starting point, so a few words are enough to create a design worth publishing. Design is now optional.

stories.title: A guide to the best website builders
stories.summary: The best WYSIWYG website builders include Hostinger AI Builder, Wix, Squarespace, Webflow, Shopify, Framer, WordPress.com, Duda, Webnode, and GoDaddy. These platforms allow users to create and edit pages visually so the published site looks like the editor. The acronym stands for what you see is what you get.

stories.title: Adobe showcases experimental tech at MAX
stories.summary: Adobe demonstrated various experimental technologies during its annual MAX conference. Researchers and engineers shared projects at the event, which the company uses to showcase its latest innovations and future directions. The presentation included a variety of technologies that are currently in the experimental phase.

stories.title: Figma explores the role of AI in creative work
stories.summary: A writer attending a design class found themselves using ChatGPT to complete assignments within ten minutes. The experience highlighted the tension between using AI to articulate personal ideas and letting the tool do the work. The goal was to crystallize thoughts, not produce a polished piece.

stories.title: Anthropic releases prompting guide for Fable 5.2
stories.summary: Anthropic has published five new rules for prompting its Fable 5.2 model. The guide is intended to assist users in interacting with the updated system. Further details are available through the company's official documentation.

stories.title: Aashish Vaishnava wins global golf design award
stories.summary: Indian golf course architect Aashish Vaishnava has become the first Indian to receive the World Golf Awards Golf Course Designer of the Year title. He shares the 2026 global award with British partner Jon Hunt. The winners were announced at a gala ceremony in Egypt.

stories.title: Workshop held to support Kashmir artisans
stories.summary: The SPVLG Artisans Foundation and the Directorate of Handicrafts and Handloom Kashmir organized a workshop to strengthen the local artisan ecosystem. Funded by the Small Industries Development Bank of India, the event brought together officials and craft experts to discuss sustainable livelihood opportunities for the region.

stories.title: Canva proposes public redesign for PIA
stories.summary: Canva has proposed a nationwide competition to rebrand Pakistan International Airlines, suggesting that ordinary citizens should shape the carrier's identity. The company says it wants to rebuild public trust through a fresh look designed by the public. The airline has not yet commented on the pitch.

stories.title: CEPT University updates BDes Hons admission criteria
stories.summary: CEPT University will accept UCEED 2027 and NID DAT 2027 scores for its five-year Bachelor of Design programme. Applicants with valid scores from these national exams will be exempt from the university's separate entrance test. The revised criteria apply to the 2027 admission cycle.

stories.title: Interior design studio focuses on cost certainty
stories.summary: Aishwarya Interiors says the shift toward luxury living in Bangalore has made clients prioritize cost certainty over style. The studio, which has delivered over 5,000 homes, now resolves design and cost together. Homeowners want to know the final price before a single panel is manufactured.

stories.title: AD Design Show 2026 returns to Mumbai
stories.summary: The AD Design Show 2026 is being held at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai from November 13 to 15. The event features brands in furniture, lighting, and decor. Organizers say the curated format allows visitors to pause and admire collections in an improved manner.

stories.title: Artistic furniture brands featured at AD Design Show
stories.summary: The AD Design Show is currently underway at the Jio World Convention Centre in Mumbai. Exhibitors include ARTSON, a studio displaying a collection called Peak ADHD. The pieces are described as hand-sculpted furniture that doubles as bold, living art inspired by organic rhythms of the outdoors.

stories.title: Hamstech opens design entrance test
stories.summary: Hamstech College of Creative Education has invited students to apply for its design entrance test. The college says the test offers a step toward pursuing creative education and professional careers. Last year, 1,500 students took the exam, with 75 receiving scholarships for their efforts.

stories.title: Ajinkya Rahane invests in Ember Cookware
stories.summary: Cricketer Ajinkya Rahane has invested in Ember Cookware, an Indian brand focused on material innovation and kitchenware design. The company says the investment marks a milestone in its growth journey. The brand spent two years researching products designed specifically for the needs of Indian kitchens.

stories.title: CEPT University accepts national design scores
stories.summary: CEPT University will accept UCEED 2027 and NID DAT 2027 scores for its BDes Hons programme. Candidates with valid scores in either exam are exempt from the university's own entrance test. Applications for the 2027 academic session are open until November 30.

stories.title: Startup raises funds for athletics sensor technology
stories.summary: Feldspar has embedded 156 sensor plates beneath a track in Cardiff to measure force data in real time. The startup is seeking up to £6 million in funding to scale the platform. It describes the system as the world's first modular platform for continuous force measurement.

stories.title: MAGIC launches AI innovation competition
stories.summary: The Marathwada Accelerator for Growth and Incubation Council has opened applications for its 2026 AI competition. The event offers 7 lakh rupees in prizes for startups and students. The organization says turning an idea into a usable solution requires more than just technology.

stories.title: Inc42 and DevX launch proptech investment fund
stories.summary: Inc42 and DevX have launched RE:FRAME, a fund with a 15 crore rupee investment pool for proptech startups. The companies note that despite a 650 billion dollar market, the real estate industry remains dependent on traditional processes like manual verification and fragmented broker networks. Change is pending.

stories.title: BabyCue wins challenge for childhood diarrhoea test
stories.summary: Odisha-based BabyCue won the Tribal Business Conclave Open Grand Challenge for DiaCue, a rapid diagnostic test for childhood diarrhoea. The startup says the tool helps distinguish between bacterial and non-bacterial infections to prevent unnecessary antibiotic use. Doctors currently make treatment decisions before test results arrive.

stories.title: Kutlerri.ai raises 4 million dollars for restaurant AI
stories.summary: Houston- and Bhubaneswar-based Kutlerri.ai raised 4 million dollars from Narahari Investments to expand its AI-powered restaurant solutions. The startup plans to scale its existing sales agent and launch three additional agents currently in beta. It uses a performance-linked pricing model to help restaurants manage operating expenses.

stories.title: Startups pitch air pollution solutions to investors
stories.summary: Twenty-eight startups pitched climate-tech solutions to venture capitalists at an AirEarth.org event. The pitches covered tracks including hydrogen, biofuels, and carbon credits. The event aimed to frame India's seasonal smog as a year-round problem for businesses to solve and for investors to back.

stories.title: Chinese high-altitude wind startup Linyi Yunchuan raises angel round - Dealroom
Nerd Gear TCG backpack hits 285,000 dollars on Kickstarter
stories.summary: Nerd Gear Gaming says its Stoneforge TCG Backpack reached its 25,000 dollar goal 12 minutes after launching on Kickstarter. The campaign has since raised over 285,000 dollars from 1,700 backers. The bag includes a removable security shell for transit and was selected as a project we love.

stories.title: Drogue raises 20 million dollars for ocean-thermal data center
stories.summary: Drogue has raised 20 million dollars to develop an ocean-thermal data center that uses seawater for server cooling and power generation. The startup plans to send a multi-megawatt prototype to sea in 2028 aboard a conventional ship. It has received preliminary approval from the American Bureau of Shipping.

stories.title: Drogue raises $20 million to power floating AI data centers with the ocean's heat - MLQ.ai
MICA celebrates faculty contributions
stories.summary: MICA is highlighting three faculty members during National Education Week to honor their dedication to teaching and artistic practice. The institution credits these educators with inspiring students to challenge conventions and pursue their creative potential. The celebration recognizes the impact of creative education beyond the classroom.

stories.title: The AI-powered ‘sea of slop’ pushing young designers out of work - Stuff.co.nz
Why was the Bauhaus school important in the history of industrial design? - Britannica
Safety standards in the baby-products market
stories.summary: Supreet Gill of Growgether says safety claims in the baby-products market are only meaningful when supported by evidence. She suggests that parents should look beyond marketing to verify that products meet recognised standards and undergo independent testing. Transparent disclosure is recommended as a guide for purchasing decisions.

stories.title: Walmart customer service prompts account cancellation
stories.summary: A New York Times writer cancelled her Walmart account after spending an hour attempting to reach a human through the retailer's customer service AI. The company is the second-biggest in the world by revenue. The incident highlights the challenges of automating support for a major brick-and-mortar retailer.

stories.title: Average daily screen time reaches 6 hours and 40 minutes
stories.summary: Research firm DemandSage reports that the average person spends 6 hours and 40 minutes a day on screens. Digital design experts suggest this habit is fueled by the visual architecture of apps. Platforms rely on calculated visual design to keep users engaged, according to university faculty.

stories.title: Librarian retires after 30-year career
stories.summary: Randle Gedeon will retire from Western Michigan University in December after 30 years of service. A professor and monographic acquisition librarian, Gedeon holds master's degrees in education and library science. He previously served at John Carroll University and Northeastern State University before joining the faculty at Western.

stories.title: BCA specialisations and career paths
stories.summary: A Bachelor of Computer Applications introduces students to programming and computer science fundamentals. Specialisations allow students to focus on fields such as artificial intelligence, gaming, or UI/UX design. The projects completed during college are intended to help shape the career paths of graduates entering the tech industry.

stories.title: StarAgile marks 10 years of professional training
stories.summary: StarAgile has trained over 300,000 professionals across 100 countries since its founding in 2016. The company, started by a former IT professional, provides training and transformation services. It is now preparing its learners for the AI era, a decade after the founder left his career.

stories.title: New specialist joins New Hanover County Extension
stories.summary: Madaleine Dishaw has been hired as a communications and support specialist for the N.C. Cooperative Extension in New Hanover County. A graduate of Briar Cliff University, Dishaw will use her background in graphic design and digital media to highlight the work of the extension and local non-profits.

research.title: AI supercharges laser physics with a stunning 250x speed boost
research.summary: Researchers at Stanford, UCLA, and SLAC have developed an AI system that simulates complex laser interactions thousands of times faster than conventional methods. The breakthrough allows scientists to predict how laser pulses behave inside special crystals in just milliseconds, without sacrificing much accuracy. This could dramatically improve the.
